question.problem:
$\,$ $x$ is rational or $x$ is negative.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(x\text{ is rational}\text{ or }x\text{ is negative}) & ≡¬((x\text{ is rational})∨(x\text{ is negative})) \\  & ≡¬(x\text{ is rational})∧¬(x\text{ is negative}) \\  & ≡(x\text{ is not rational})∧(x\text{ is not negative}) \\  & ≡x\text{ is not rational}\text{ and }x\text{ is not negative}.\end{aligned}
$$
